Package com.signalwire.sdk.swml

Enum Class Codec

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<Codec>
com.signalwire.sdk.swml.Codec
All Implemented Interfaces:
WireEnum, Serializable, Comparable<Codec>, Constable
public enum Codec extends Enum<Codec> implements WireEnum
Media codec for the SWML tap verb, as a typed, compile-time-checked closed set.

The Python reference FunctionResult.tap validates codec against ["PCMU", "PCMA"] and raises ValueError on anything else. The methods that take a tap codec (FunctionResult.tap(String, String, String, Codec)) accept this enum or a plain String. The enum gives editor autocompletion and makes a typo fail at compile time (a bare string like "PCMX" only fails at runtime, on the server). Strings keep parity with the Python reference (which uses a bare str): 


 result.tap("wss://x", "t1", "both", Codec.PCMA);   // typed, autocompleted
 result.tap("wss://x", "t1", "both", "PCMA");       // string still works (parity)

This is the SWAIG tap codec set only — do NOT reuse it for RELAY stream/connect. RELAY device codecs are a much larger superset (e.g. PCMU,PCMA,OPUS,G729,G722,VP8,H264, comma-joined); the 2-value SWAIG tap codec set is deliberately distinct and never shared.

The wire strings are upper-case ("PCMU" / "PCMA"), matching the reference's literal list exactly. Each constant's value is the canonical wire string, so routing a tap through the enum is byte-for-byte identical to passing that string.

    • fromWire

      public static Codec fromWire(String wire)
      Parse a wire string into a Codec, or return null if it is not a recognised codec. Matching is exact (case-sensitive), mirroring the reference's literal in ["PCMU", "PCMA"] check (so "pcmu" returns null). The Java analog of Rust's from_str.
      Parameters:
      wire - the candidate wire string (case-sensitive).
      Returns:
      the matching constant, or null if none matches.
